info.name: ParlayAPI: sports odds, props and prediction markets
info.description:
Real-time sports odds from 30+ sportsbooks and data sources, across 90+ sport
keys: moneylines, spreads, totals, player props, arbitrage and positive EV
boards, historical closing lines from 2005, and prediction markets (Kalshi,
Polymarket).

## Run it right now, with no key

Open folder **1. Getting started** and press Send. Those seven requests need
no API key, no signup and no credit card. They hit live production.

## Then add a key

A free key is 1,000 credits per month with no card at
https://parlay-api.com/signup . Paste it into the `api_key` collection
variable (Collection > Variables) and the other five folders start working.
Auth is an `X-API-Key` header, set once at collection level.

`?apiKey=` as a query parameter and `Authorization: Bearer <key>` both work
too, if either fits your stack better.

## Collection variables

| Variable | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `base_url` | https://parlay-api.com | API host. |
| `api_key` | (empty) | Your key. Keyless folder works without it. |
| `sport_key` | americanfootball_nfl | Any key from GET /v1/sports. |
| `event_id` | (an NFL Week 1 game) | Refresh from GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/events. |
| `player` | Patrick Mahomes | Partial name match for the props search. |
| `asset` | BTC | Asset for the crypto prediction markets. |
| `date` | a recent date | YYYY-MM-DD for the historical requests. |

Change `sport_key` once and most of the collection follows.

## Good to know

- Credits are per endpoint and the odds endpoints scale with markets and
  regions. The catalogue is `GET /v1/meta/credit-costs` and the tier table is
  at https://parlay-api.com/pricing .
- The odds response shape is drop-in compatible with the-odds-api's /v4
  endpoints, so an existing integration usually only needs a new base URL and
  key.
- Streaming (WebSocket and SSE) is a Business-tier and up feature and is not
  in this collection, because Postman is not a streaming client. The
  streaming contract is described in /v1/asyncapi.json.
- Full machine-readable spec: https://parlay-api.com/openapi.json .
  Browseable docs: https://parlay-api.com/docs .

Canonical copy of this file, always current:
https://parlay-api.com/collections/ParlayAPI.postman_collection.json

item.name: 1. Getting started (no API key)
item.description:
Every request in this folder runs with no API key and no signup. Hit Send
right now.

The `/v1/try/*` endpoints are the keyless demo: real live prices, capped at
the first 5 events per sport and 60 requests per hour per IP. The response
nests the games under an `events` key and carries a `demo_remaining_hour`
counter so you can see the budget you have left.

When you want all events, all books and all markets, a free key is 1,000
credits per month with no card: https://parlay-api.com/signup . Paste it into the
`api_key` collection variable and every other folder starts working.

request.description:
The fastest possible look at the data. No key, no signup, real prices from
30+ sportsbooks and data sources.

Games come back under the `events` key, each with a `bookmakers` array
holding one entry per book and its markets. `demo_remaining_hour` tells you
how many of the 60 hourly demo calls are left for your IP.

Change `sport_key` (a collection variable) to any key from
`GET /v1/sports`: americanfootball_nfl, basketball_nba, baseball_mlb,
icehockey_nhl, soccer_epl, mma_mixed_martial_arts, and 90+ more.

The keyed equivalent, with every event and every market, is
`GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/odds` in the Odds folder.

Cross-book arbitrage on the demo slice: pairs of prices where backing both
sides locks a profit regardless of result.

Each row names the two books, the two prices, the stake split and the profit
percentage. Empty array is a normal and honest answer: clean two-way arbs on
five events are rare, and the keyed endpoint scanning every event is where
they turn up.

Keyed version with filters (minProfit, exclude_books, markets):
`GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/arbitrage`.

Positive expected value picks on the demo slice: soft-book prices measured
against a sharp book's no-vig line, which is the standard way to estimate
whether a price is actually beatable.

Each row carries the offered price, the fair price, the edge percentage and
the books compared. Keyed version lets you choose the sharp book and the
minimum edge: `GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/ev`.

Middle opportunities on the demo slice: two books offering spreads or totals
far enough apart that a range of results wins both sides.

Rows carry the two lines, the gap and the win window. Keyed version:
`GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/middles`.

The catalogue: 90+ sport keys with their titles, groups and whether they are
currently in season. No key required.

This is the lookup for the `sport_key` collection variable. Every odds,
props, historical and prediction-market request in this collection takes one
of these keys.

Every sportsbook, DFS app, exchange and prediction market we collect, with
its key, title and region. No key required.

Use the `key` values in the `bookmakers=` query parameter on the odds, props
and closing-line endpoints to pin a response to the books you care about.

A public JSON feed of the largest recent line movements across the board, the
same data behind the /moves page on the site. No key required, no credits.

Handy as a zero-setup smoke test that the collection is wired up, and as a
cheap way to see whether the data looks alive before you sign up.

item.name: 2. Odds
item.description:
Game lines: moneyline (h2h), spreads and totals across every book we
collect, plus the derived boards (best line, arbitrage, positive EV) built on
top of them.

These need an API key in the `api_key` collection variable. Free tier is
1,000 credits per month with no card: https://parlay-api.com/signup . Per-endpoint
credit costs are in `GET /v1/meta/credit-costs`, and the tier table is at
https://parlay-api.com/pricing .

query.description: Comma-separated book regions: us, us2, uk, eu, au.
american or decimal. Decimal is the default.
Comma-separated book keys from GET /v1/bookmakers. Overrides regions.
Shortcut for one UTC day, YYYY-MM-DD.

request.description:
The core endpoint. Every upcoming event for a sport, with one entry per
bookmaker and one price per outcome.

`markets` takes any comma-separated combination of h2h (moneyline), spreads
and totals. `regions` picks the book set (us, us2, uk, eu, au); `bookmakers`
overrides it with explicit keys. `oddsFormat` is decimal by default, american
if you ask.

Response shape is drop-in compatible with the-odds-api's /v4 odds endpoint,
so an existing integration usually only needs the base URL and the key
swapped.

Cost scales with markets and regions, so ask for what you need: see
`GET /v1/meta/credit-costs`.

query.description: ISO 8601 lower bound on start time.
ISO 8601 upper bound on start time.

request.description:
The schedule without any prices: event id, home and away team, and commence
time.

Cheap way to find the `event_id` you need for the single-event odds call
below, and the right endpoint to poll when you are building a slate view and
do not want to pay for odds you are not showing yet.

query.description: Required. Comma-separated: us, us2, uk, eu, au.

request.description:
Every book's prices for a single game. Use this instead of the full-sport
call when you already know which event you care about: it is the difference
between pulling one game and pulling a whole slate.

`event_id` is a collection variable pre-filled with a real NFL Week 1 game.
Event ids do not live forever, so when this returns 404 grab a fresh one from
the Upcoming events request above.

`regions` is required on this endpoint.

query.description: Restrict the comparison to these book keys.

request.description:
Line shopping in one call: for each outcome, the book offering the best
price right now, and what that price is worth against the field.

This is the request that makes the case for an aggregator. The same
moneyline can differ by several cents between books, and over a season that
gap is the whole margin.

query.description: CSV of market keys to scan.
CSV of book keys to drop from either side.

request.description:
Every two-sided price pair on the board that locks a profit, sorted best
first, with the stake split already computed.

`minProfit` filters out the noise floor. `exclude_books` is worth knowing
about: exchange asks (novig, prophetx) can be thin, so an arb anchored on one
may not be fillable at size. `markets` narrows the scan to game lines or to
specific prop markets.

item.name: Positive EV against a sharp book

query.description: Sharp book used as the fair-odds baseline.
CSV of market keys, including player_* prop markets.

request.description:
Soft-book prices measured against a sharp book's no-vig line. Rows carry the
offered price, the implied fair price, the edge percentage and how many books
were compared.

`sharpBook` defaults to pinnacle. `minEdge` sets the floor in percent, and
`min_books` drops rows where too few books priced the market for the
consensus to mean much.

How a price got where it is: the timestamped movement history for a market,
optionally narrowed to one event, one book or one player.

`hours` is the lookback window. Steam detection, opener-to-current deltas and
"who moved first" analysis all start here.

item.name: 3. Player props
item.description:
Player props with American odds from sportsbooks, DFS apps (PrizePicks,
Underdog, Sleeper and friends) and exchanges, in one normalized shape.

DFS apps do not quote two-sided odds the way a sportsbook does, so
`dfsOdds=midpoint` normalizes them to a zero-vig +100/-100 pair by default.
Pass `dfsOdds=effective` if you would rather see each app's own implied
price.

query.description: One entry per prop with a books[] array. Recommended.

request.description:
Every player prop currently priced for a sport. `grouped=true` returns one
entry per prop with a `books[]` array, which is what you want for line
shopping; leave it off and you get one flat row per book per prop.

`markets` takes any comma-separated player_* keys. Full list per sport comes
from the prop markets request below, or from `GET /v1/markets`.

Responses can be large. `limit` and `offset` paginate; `maxAgeSec` drops
rows staler than you are willing to trade on.

query.description: One entry per prop with a books[] array.

request.description:
The same endpoint narrowed to a single player by partial name match. This is
the shape most prop tools actually ship: a search box, then every book's
price for that player's markets side by side.

`player` is a collection variable so you can change it once and re-run.

item.name: Prop markets offered for a sport

request.description:
Which player_* market keys are actually live for this sport right now, so you
can build the `markets=` filter from data instead of guessing.

NFL gives you passing, rushing, receiving, anytime touchdown and kicking
markets; NBA gives points, rebounds, assists and the combination markets;
MLB gives strikeouts, hits, total bases and more.

item.name: 4. Historical and closing lines
item.description:
The archive: game-line closing odds from 2005, and 30M+ player prop closing
lines since 2022.

Closing lines are the benchmark serious bettors grade against, because a
strategy that consistently beats the close is the one that holds up over a
large sample. The CLV request at the bottom of this folder does that grading
for you.

Free-tier keys have a short lookback window, so start with the coverage
request (no key needed) to see what the archive holds before you commit to a
tier: https://parlay-api.com/pricing .

query.description: Only list sports with at least this many rows.

request.description:
How deep the archive actually goes, per sport: row counts, date span,
contributing sources and score-coverage percentage. Public, no key, no
credits.

Run this before you plan a backtest. It answers "do you have enough of my
sport, far enough back" with numbers instead of marketing copy.

item.name: Historical odds snapshot for a date

request.description:
The board as it stood on a given day. Pass `date=YYYY-MM-DD` for a single
day out of the long-term archive, which also carries the anchored
closing-line variants (book keys suffixed `_an`).

Omit `date` and you get the most recent snapshot. Note that the single-date
path and the dateFrom/dateTo range path read different stores and can return
different rows for the same day; the single-date path is the archival one.

item.name: Closing odds for a date range

query.description: Season filter for game lines, e.g. 2025-26.

request.description:
Closing lines in bulk: game lines from the historical odds archive, player
props from the prop closing-line archive, over any date range or season.

Pass a `player_*` key in `markets` to pull prop closes instead of game lines.
`season` (for example 2025-26) is a shortcut for a full season of game lines.
Paginate with `limit` and `offset`.

This is the endpoint model backtests are built on.

The last price each book showed before each match started, for the last few
days. Pinnacle by default, since Pinnacle's close is the usual sharp
reference.

`daysFrom` is the lookback in days, bounded by your plan. For anything older
than that window, use the closing-odds request above.

item.name: Grade a bet slip for closing line value

request.description:
Send the bets you took and get back what they were worth against the closing
line: per-bet `clv_cents` and `clv_pct`, no-vig adjusted where both sides
closed, plus an aggregate summary.

Works for game lines (send home_team and away_team) and for player props
(send player, market and line). `taken_odds` is your actual fill in American
odds. `sharp_book` defaults to pinnacle and falls back to novig when Pinnacle
did not price the market.

Edit the example body: it is a two-bet slip, one prop and one moneyline.

body.raw:
{
  "bets": [
    {
      "sport_key": "americanfootball_nfl",
      "game_date": "2026-01-11",
      "player": "Patrick Mahomes",
      "market": "player_pass_yds",
      "outcome": "over",
      "line": 274.5,
      "taken_odds": -110
    },
    {
      "sport_key": "americanfootball_nfl",
      "game_date": "2026-01-11",
      "home_team": "Kansas City Chiefs",
      "away_team": "Buffalo Bills",
      "market": "h2h",
      "outcome": "Kansas City Chiefs",
      "line": null,
      "taken_odds": -135
    }
  ],
  "sharp_book": "pinnacle"
}

item.name: 5. Prediction markets
item.description:
Kalshi and Polymarket prices alongside the sportsbook board, in the same
normalized shape as everything else.

Prediction markets settle in dollars rather than in odds, so a contract
trading at 0.62 is the market's 62% probability. Reading them next to a
sportsbook price is one of the cleaner edges available right now, and the
divergence feed at the bottom of this folder is exactly that comparison,
free and keyless.

Two of the four requests here need no key: the keyword search and the
divergence feed.

request.description:
Current Kalshi and Polymarket contracts for a sport, with yes/no bid, ask,
mid-market implied probability, volume and open interest.

`sources` narrows to one venue. Pair the implied probabilities here with
`GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/consensus` to see where the exchanges and the
books disagree.

item.name: Search prediction markets by keyword, no key

query.description: Search terms. Percent-encode spaces as %20 for phrases.
Comma-separated venues. Novig is also accepted but its public endpoint is refusing requests at the moment, so the example pins the two that answer.
Drop contracts below this traded volume.

request.description:
Keyword search across the prediction-market venues we collect, and it needs no API key.
Prediction-market contracts are titled in prose, not in team keys, so search
is usually the right way in.

The example searches `afc` because a conference-winner futures market is one
of the few things both Kalshi and Polymarket price, so one request shows you
both venues side by side. Single-word terms keep the raw URL clean; if you
search a phrase, percent-encode the space as `%20`.

`sources` narrows the venues. `min_volume` filters out untraded contracts,
which is worth doing: a market with no volume has a price but not an opinion.
`sort` accepts balanced, volume or confidence.

First call for a term fans out to the venues live, so expect several
seconds; the answer is cached for 90 seconds after that and comes back
immediately. `cache_hit` in the response tells you which one you got.

query.description: all, price_above, price_range, direction_15m, direction_1h, direction_daily.

request.description:
Kalshi crypto price markets for an asset: the price ladders
(`price_at_or_above` per strike, and `price_range` bands) with bid, ask,
implied probability, volume and open interest.

`asset` is a collection variable, pre-filled with BTC. `market_type` filters
the ladder family. Ask for a combination outside the live window and you get
a 404 naming what is live, with no credit charged, rather than a billed empty
array.

item.name: Books vs prediction markets divergence, no key

request.description:
A public JSON feed of the widest current gaps between sportsbook implied
probability and prediction-market implied probability, the same data behind
the /divergence board on the site. No key, no credits.

The clearest one-request demonstration of why having both sides in one API
is useful.

item.name: 6. Meta and status
item.description:
The endpoints you wire up once and then forget: what everything costs, what
the platform is doing, and how much of your quota is left.

All of these except account usage are keyless.

request.description:
Machine-readable platform status: per-source collection health and the
freshness of what we are serving. No key required.

Worth polling from a monitoring job if you have a pipeline that depends on
fresh odds, so a stale-source problem shows up as an alert rather than as a
bad bet.

item.name: Credit cost of every endpoint, no key

request.description:
The full cost catalogue: what each endpoint charges, which ones are free, and
the formulas behind the variable-cost ones (odds calls scale with markets and
regions).

Read this before you write a polling loop. The same costs are published as
`x-credit-cost` extensions in /openapi.json, so SDK generators and agents can
pick them up automatically. Tier limits are at
https://parlay-api.com/pricing .

item.name: API info and discovery URLs, no key

request.description:
The discovery document: spec URLs (/openapi.json, /v1/asyncapi.json),
documentation links, SDK packages and the endpoint families available. No key
required.

This is the request an AI agent makes first when it lands on the API, and it
is a fast way for a human to see the whole surface at once.

Credits used, credits remaining, reset date and current tier for the key in
the `api_key` variable.

Free tier is 1,000 credits per month with no card. Check this in your own
integration before a big pull so you find the ceiling in your logs rather
than in a 402.

variable.description: API host. Leave as is. https://api.parlay-api.com is the same surface on a host that bypasses the CDN edge, for high-volume callers.
Your ParlayAPI key. Empty on purpose: folder 1 runs without one. Get a free key, 1,000 credits per month and no card, at https://parlay-api.com/signup . Sent as the X-API-Key header.
Any key from GET /v1/sports: basketball_nba, baseball_mlb, icehockey_nhl, soccer_epl, mma_mixed_martial_arts, and 90+ more.
An NFL Week 1 game. Event ids expire once the game is old, so refresh from GET /v1/sports/{sport_key}/events.
Partial name match for the player props search.
Asset for the Kalshi crypto prediction markets.
YYYY-MM-DD for the historical requests. Free-tier keys have a short lookback window, so keep this recent until you upgrade.
